title: CBPL-kit: a web-based interactive toolkit for ternary phase equilibrium and liquid-liquid extraction
description:
CBPL-kit turns the measurements students take in a liquid-liquid extraction experiment into a quantitative and reproducible analysis. The Hunter–Nash construction, normally carried out by hand on the ternary phase diagram, is performed numerically, so an operating condition can be changed and the result seen immediately rather than redrawn from scratch.

The toolkit links two complementary workflows. From raw equilibrium and tie-line data for a ternary system, it fits the binodal curve, recovers the full tie-line compositions, constructs the conjugate curve and estimates the plait point, reports the distribution coefficients and selectivity, and checks the internal consistency of the tie-lines with the Othmer–Tobias, Hand, and Bachman correlations. From a student's own run — titration data and flow rates — it steps off the equilibrium stages, verifies the mass balance independently by the lever rule, and lets the solvent-to-feed (S/F) ratio and the feed composition be explored across their operable spans.

The application runs entirely in the browser through Pyodide, requiring no installation, account, or server-side computation, and the same Python modules can be imported in a notebook. Seven ternary systems are bundled, and users can enter their own measured data for any Type I system. Developed for the Chemical and Biological Process Laboratory (CBPL) course in the Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering at Seoul National University.
